## Reading Order on Synthetic Pages

A. Author and B. Writer

## 1 Introduction

Documents set in two columns are read down the left column first and then down the right one. A model that orders lines must learn where one column ends and the next one begins, even when a short last line sits beside the other column.

## 2 Related Work

Earlier systems cut the page at its widest gaps, first across and then down, which works for clean pages but fails on ragged layouts.

## 3 Method

We score every pair of lines with a small network and decode an order from the pairwise scores. Lines that belong together, such as the tumorigenesis example, form one block.

## 4 Results

The decoded order matches the true order on most pages; errors cluster around captions and footnotes.
